review_notes: Independently read the complete current proposal.json, functionality.md, fact-dispositions.json and link-dispositions.json, all owned canonical/rendered source pages, all 30 subjects and all 36 outgoing baseline links.
All six proposed writes address owned function subjects and are supported by canonical definitions or consumers. The proposal contains no new links, entities, merges or follow-ups.
COPY_ATTRS copies into existing dat_attrs storage; PUSH_ATTRS separately copies into dat_attrs_backup and installs that pointer. Both proposed attribute corrections are necessary and supported.

OnDamage's ordered fan-out, guarded article references, secondary-death installations and state-dependent Thunder effects agree with the inspected callees. The replacement appropriately withdraws the baseline's universal teardown guarantee.
Pickup and drop proposals accurately describe the heavy-item exclusion, numeric switch cases, default branch, conditional flags and -1 argument without inventing gameplay categories.

The absorption proposal correctly distinguishes finite representable float-to-int conversion from exceptional conversions. The subsequent int-to-float assignment can round large integer values; neither proposal nor retained dispositions should be read as guaranteeing exact preservation of every representable int.

The current ledgers appropriately defer the broad controllable-Thunder fact and principal-projectile/component link that the earlier librarian had retained. Acceptance applies to the current top-level proposal, not the earlier embedded proposal.

Canonical Release callbacks are shared by Hold and Release table entries. Rendered Hold aliases do not establish exclusive Hold semantics. Article registration is independently verified; the rendered parts-helper alias remains deferred.
Acceptance does not resolve compiled section membership, full gameplay aliases, resource lifetime or deeper presentation-helper semantics.
